subject: Capacity commitment & bursting playbook for FastPay month-end spikes
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fastpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@fastpay.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity commitments for FastPay large-batch settlement spikes

Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. FastPay runs nightly settlement batches that produce 10–15x traffic spikes for ~45–90 minutes at the end of our processing window. We’re evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace our self-hosted stack, but two sticking points for procurement and our ops team:

- Can Redwood guarantee latency SLOs during those bursts if we buy reserved GPUs? We need a concrete uptime/latency commitment (p99 < 200ms for generation) for committed capacity or a documented exception playbook when bursts exceed reserved slots.
- How does queueing/prioritization work for reserved capacity? Specifically we want to know if FastPay requests can jump ahead of best-effort tenants or if requests are strictly FIFO across customers on a host.
- What is the expected headroom you recommend (percent of committed GPUs) to keep SLA violations < 0.1%?

Procurement prefers to see an operational playbook and an explicit amendment to the Dedicated contract describing bursting behavior and any exceptions (cost, fallback models, throttling). Can you share a draft? Also need an estimate of the monthly cost delta for 8 reserved A100s with 30% dedicated headroom.

Appreciate any details you can share — Sara and I will route internally once we have a formal proposal.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fastpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity commitments for FastPay large-batch settlement spikes

Tom —

Thanks for the clear summary. That use case is exactly where our Dedicated product shines, and we can accommodate a formal amendment for bursting behavior. I’m looping Ben (sales engineering) and Marissa (runtime SRE) to give technical and ops details.

High level we can offer:
- Reserved slots: dedicate 8 GPUs to FastPay with guaranteed baseline throughput for pinned model versions.
- Headroom: we typically recommend 20–30% additional uncommitted capacity or an autoscale burst pool. For the p99 target you quoted, our initial estimate is 25% headroom for your observed spike profile, but Marissa will confirm after she reviews your latency histograms.
- Queueing/prioritization: we support per-tenant priority queues on dedicated pools; FastPay can be configured as "priority=high" which routes requests ahead of lower-priority tenants on the same physical cluster. It does not preempt in-progress tokens but does reorder scheduling for queued requests.
- Playbook: attached is a first draft of our "bursting playbook" that outlines fallback routing (smaller quantized model), priority queue behavior, and cost implications.

Ben and Marissa — can you confirm headroom recommendation and the expected cost delta for 8 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs with 25–30% burst buffer? I’ve attached the draft playbook.

Next step: if FastPay is comfortable, we can create a contract amendment (DocuSign) that lists the SLA terms, headroom, and the month-end priority exception clause your procurement asked for.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
attachments: fastpay-burst-playbook-v1.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Capacity commitments — queue behavior & headroom calc

Eve/Marissa — forwarding a short tech note for the playbook and numbers. Summary below; see appendix (redwood-queue-appendix.md) for microbenchmarks.

Summary:
- Queueing: On Dedicated pools we implement per-tenant queues ordered by priority, then arrival. Priority is a 3-level enum (high/normal/low). High-priority requests are placed in a separate dispatch queue and scheduled ahead of normal, but we do not preempt running tokens. That means transient p99 hiccups can still occur if a large request is already in progress.
- Headroom calc (rough): baseline committed capacity = 8 GPUs x median throughput (tokens/sec) for your model. Measured spike factor: 12x for 30–60 minutes during your sample. To maintain p99 < 200ms we recommend: 8 reserved GPUs + a 2-GPU burst pool (25%) + autoscale buffer that can spin up 2 more GPUs (on-demand) within 90s.
- Expected SLA impact: with this configuration we project < 0.05% SLA breach during typical spikes and < 0.25% during pathological month-end > 12x spikes without additional mitigation.
- Cost delta (back-of-envelope): reserve 8 A100 equiv = $XX,XXX/month; 2-GPU burst pool reserved = +$X,XXX/month; on-demand autoscale usage billed as used — estimate $4k–$6k for typical month-end spikes. We’ll produce exact numbers for procurement.

Action items: Marissa — can you confirm the 90s spin-up estimate and whether we should propose a hard cap on concurrent autoscale for the amendment? Also, should the contract include a clause that documents model fallback (quantized variant) as an automatic mitigation step?

—Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-queue-appendix.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fastpay.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@fastpay.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity commitments for FastPay large-batch settlement spikes

Tom / Sara —

I reviewed FastPay’s histogram and Ben’s appendix. Confirming the operational proposal and a few clarifications to include in the amendment:

1) Guaranteed baseline: 8 dedicated GPUs pinned to your account for the specified model versions. FastPay will have exclusive scheduling slots on those GPUs for queued work (subject to live migrations for maintenance).

2) Priority queueing: FastPay requests will be assigned "high" priority on the dedicated pool. High-priority requests are scheduled before normal traffic when queued but will not cancel in-flight work. This reduces queuing latency for short requests; long-running token generation still uses the same runtime slots.

3) Burst policy (month-end exception):
- 2-GPU warm burst pool reserved and kept in standby (lower-cost reservation) for low-latency spin-up.
- Autoscale: additional on-demand GPUs can be provisioned up to 2 more (soft cap) and are typically available within ~90 seconds in our fastest cloud region.
- Fallback: if capacity is saturated we will route a percentage of new requests to a quantized model (same topology, lower precision) with a documented quality delta. FastPay can opt-out of fallback in writing.

4) SLA language we propose to include in amendment:
- Committed throughput SLO: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 200ms for requests served on reserved capacity under baseline load.
- Burst window exception: for pre-notified month-end windows, Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to keep p99 < 200ms; if spikes exceed the combined reserved+burst pool, we will apply fallback routing. Any SLA credit for breaches during unplanned pathological spikes will be evaluated per the amendment terms.

5) Cost: precise pricing for reserved burst pool and autoscale will be in the commercial appendix. Initial estimate per Ben stands; I’ll send a procurement-ready quote by EOD.

If that aligns with FastPay, we can produce an amendment (DocuSign) and a brief operational runbook for your SREs to validate during a staging run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fastpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@fastpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity commitments for FastPay large-batch settlement spikes

Evelyn/Marissa/Ben —

Thanks for the quick, detailed responses and the draft playbook. This is exactly what procurement needed. A few quick notes:

- The fallback to a quantized model is acceptable as long as we get clear metrics on the quality delta and a rollback plan; please include that in the appendix.
- For month-end we will pre-notify Redwood 72 hours in advance and request the month-end exception window to be honored.
- Procurements asks for an explicit clause that caps the autoscale exposure (we prefer a hard cap of 2 on-demand GPUs on top of the reserved+burst pool). Please include the hard cap and the costs.

Assuming those are in the amendment, FastPay will sign. Please send the DocuSign link and the final numbers and we’ll route to legal.

Appreciate it.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay
